title: Reduce streaming token latency: kernel scheduling + KV cache hot-path + adaptive flush/backpressure
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: Streaming token generation latency is a top customer pain point for low-latency chat use-cases. This PR applies a set of coordinated changes across kernel scheduling, the KV-cache hot-path, and continuous-batching/flush cadence to reduce median and tail per-token latency for streaming responses. Motivation: customers reported 50-200ms token stalls under bursty small-request workloads (incidents: SUP-4123). The root causes were (1) suboptimal kernel scheduling that caused small single-token workloads to wait behind long kernel dispatches, (2) KV cache reads/writes on the hot-path that allocated/locked per-token, and (3) a conservative flush cadence and rigid backpressure logic that increased inter-token spacing under partial batches. Summary of changes: 1) Kernel scheduling: introduce priority-aware fast-path for short token-generation kernels and non-blocking kernel dispatch for small requests. Added a lightweight token-priority queue and early preemption for long-running kernels. 2) KV cache: refactor KV cache hot-path to use lock-free read fast-path (per-shard read-copy) and reduce allocations by reusing slab-allocated buffers; added microbenchmarks and correctness asserts. 3) Continuous batching & flush cadence: implement adaptive flush cadence that measures queue latency and dynamically lowers flush interval for small-batch workloads; improved backpressure heuristics to avoid full-queue stalls by allowing opportunistic partial flushes when latency SLOs degrade. 4) Metrics & observability: new per-request token latency metric, kernel-sched histogram, KV-cache hit/miss timing, and an end-to-end streaming latency dashboard. Benchmarks: microbench (gpt2-small synthetic) shows median per-token latency improvement: 24% (from 48ms -> 36.5ms) and p95 improvement: 31% (from 120ms -> 83ms) under bursty single-token workloads. End-to-end on internal chat load (75% small messages) showed median token latency down 18% and p95 down 25%. Backwards compatibility: no API changes; all changes gated behind runtime flags and rollout will be canaried. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for KV-cache fast-path - [x] Integration tests for streaming correctness - [x] Microbench harness updates - [x] End-to-end perf dashboard panels - [x] Feature-flag and rollout plan
